name: Elasticsearch
tagline: Lucene-based distributed search and analytics engine for text, vectors, logs and metrics.
description: Elasticsearch is the distributed search engine that made Lucene easy to cluster, and it remains the default choice for application search, log analytics and security analytics at large scale. Recent releases lean hard into AI retrieval: dense and sparse vectors, BBQ quantization, semantic_text fields with built-in inference, and hybrid ranking via retrievers. Since late 2024 the source is available under AGPL-3.0 alongside SSPL and the Elastic License, which ended the 'not open source' debate that spawned OpenSearch. Expect to spend real effort on shard sizing, mappings and JVM tuning, or pay Elastic to do it in Elastic Cloud.

license.name: AGPL-3.0, SSPL 1.0 or Elastic License 2.0 (your choice)

pricing.notes: Self-managed free tier covers core search, security and vectors; Platinum/Enterprise subscriptions add ML and advanced features. Elastic Cloud is resource-based (Hosted) or usage-based (Serverless) with a free trial.

scale.notes: Shards and replicas spread across nodes automatically; cross-cluster replication and cross-cluster search handle multi-region. Multi-PB logging clusters are common.

strengths: Best-in-class relevance tooling: BM25, analyzers, synonyms, learning-to-rank and hybrid retrievers
Native dense, sparse (ELSER) and quantized (BBQ) vector search in the same index as text
ES|QL gives a piped query language for logs, metrics and joins against lookup indices
Huge ecosystem: Kibana, Beats, Logstash, Elastic Agent and clients for every language
AGPL option makes it open source again for teams that care about OSI licensing
weaknesses: Shard count, heap and mapping design need ongoing expert tuning
Near-real-time refresh means writes are not instantly searchable and there are no multi-document transactions
Advanced features (ML, cross-cluster replication, some security) require paid tiers
Resource hungry compared with Meilisearch, Typesense or object-storage engines like Quickwit
useCases: E-commerce and site search with faceting
Hybrid keyword plus semantic retrieval for RAG
notIdealFor: Small apps that just need typo-tolerant search box
Cheap long-term log archival at PB scale
